<objective>
Make the phase's own records true.

Three documents describe a state that stopped being current weeks ago, and each of them is what a
future reader will trust instead of re-deriving the truth:

- `01-UAT.md` records test 1 as `result: issue / severity: blocker` for a cold-start failure that
  commit `55f3b69` fixed on 2026-07-30. Its own Gap Reconciliation section already says so
  ("G-01-1 — resolved (already)"), and the test entry was never updated.
- `01-VERIFICATION.md` still carries `status: gaps_found`, `score: 7/11 must-haves verified`, and a
  `gaps:` block listing three items that commits `f29ece0` and `8487bfd` and the two AST coverage
  guards closed. `01-UAT.md`'s own Notes section flags it: "01-VERIFICATION.md is stale …
  Re-verification is queued for after this UAT pass."
- `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` shows all eight ACCT rows as `Gaps Found` with unticked boxes. The
  verifier set that deliberately and said it "should stay until the gaps above close" — so the
  correct move is per-requirement adjudication, not a bulk flip in either direction.

And UAT test 26, the goal-backward outcome roll-up, sits at `[pending]` for one specific reason: its
item 1 is PARTIAL because creating the second venue from the UI was blocked by G-01-7, so the
multi-currency creation leg was reached by seeding a row rather than by the owner's own hands. Plans
01-14 through 01-16 remove that blocker; this plan closes the roll-up on top of them.

**As a** developer picking this project up in three months, **I want to** read the phase's records
and find them true, **so that** I do not either re-fix something already fixed or ship on top of
something recorded as done that never was.

Purpose: the failure mode this plan guards against is its own — a reconciliation that over-corrects.
Every edit here has to cite the check that justifies it, and anything resting on an unrun human
check stays exactly as it is.

Output: an evidence ledger, three corrected documents, an adjudicated requirements table, and the
outcome roll-up finally answerable.
</objective>

<standing_execution_overrides>
1. **This plan changes no application code.** If a check in Task 1 fails, the correct outcome is a
   ledger row recording that it failed and a document that keeps saying so — not a code fix smuggled
   into a documentation plan. Raise it in the summary instead.
2. **Never run `pnpm dev`.** Use `pnpm build`, `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm exec vitest run`,
   `pnpm lint`. The suite is evidence here, so run it and record the real file and test counts —
   never a recalled number.
3. **`.env.local` is gitignored**; recreate it from `/opt/homebrew/bin/supabase status` before
   running the suite or `tests/setup-env.ts` hard-fails.
4. **Use `Edit`, never `Write`, on all four existing documents.** A whole-file `Write` on
   `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `01-UAT.md` or `01-VERIFICATION.md` destroys content outside the diff window,
   and these files are long. `01-RECONCILIATION.md` is the only new file and is the only `Write`.
5. **Never `npx tsc` / `pnpm dlx tsc`.** Use `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`.
6. **Snapshot directory: `/tmp/gsd-01-17/`, and it is WRITE-ONCE.** Task 1 copies all three existing
   documents there before doing anything else, creating the directory with `mkdir` (no `-p`) so a
   second attempt fails rather than overwriting. Tasks 2 and 3 diff against those copies rather than
   against `HEAD`, and never re-take them. Write-once is what makes the preservation guards real: a
   snapshot re-taken after editing has begun is a baseline of the edited file, and every check
   against it passes while protecting nothing. The path is a literal, not a shell variable: each acceptance-criteria
   command runs in its own shell, so a `SCRATCH=$(mktemp -d)` would be empty by the time the
   criterion runs. Nothing under `/tmp` can be committed by accident, which is the other reason it
   lives there rather than inside `.planning/`. **Why not `git diff`/`git status` as the baseline:**
   the working tree may already be dirty for reasons that predate this plan — at plan time
   `01-UAT.md` carried an uncommitted work-in-progress diff — and a git baseline would attribute
   those edits to this plan and fail a correct execution.
7. **BSD `wc` pads its output.** On macOS `wc -l` prints leading spaces, so `… | wc -l | grep -qx 0`
   never matches and silently fails a correct edit. Every `wc -l` gate in this plan is written
   `… | wc -l | tr -d ' ' | grep -qx 0`; keep the `tr` if you touch one.

Migrations `0001`–`0007` are applied and must not be edited.
</standing_execution_overrides>

    **First, snapshot all three documents — WRITE-ONCE.** Before reading or writing anything else,
    run exactly this. `mkdir` without `-p` is the write-once primitive: it fails if the directory
    already exists, so the `cp`s are unreachable on any re-run.

    ```
    mkdir /tmp/gsd-01-17 || { echo "SNAPSHOT ALREADY EXISTS — refusing to overwrite. See recovery note."; exit 1; }
    cp .planning/phases/01-multi-tenant-foundation/01-UAT.md          /tmp/gsd-01-17/01-UAT.before
    cp .planning/phases/01-multi-tenant-foundation/01-VERIFICATION.md /tmp/gsd-01-17/01-VERIFICATION.before
    cp .planning/REQUIREMENTS.md                                     /tmp/gsd-01-17/REQUIREMENTS.before
    ```

    These three files are the baseline for every preservation check in Tasks 2 and 3, and for this
    task's own "no document was touched" assertion. The baseline is a snapshot rather than `HEAD`
    because the working tree may already carry unrelated uncommitted edits to these files — it did at
    plan time, with a work-in-progress diff on `01-UAT.md` already adding lines containing
    `MIS-DERIVED` and `mobile friendly`. A `git diff`/`git status` baseline would attribute those to
    this plan and fail a correct execution.

    **Why write-once and not merely "Tasks 2 and 3 must not re-take it."** The dangerous case is a
    re-run of THIS task after Task 2 has already begun editing: a plain `cp` would overwrite the
    `.before` files with already-edited documents, after which this task's `cmp -s` gate passes
    vacuously and Task 2's `MIS-DERIVED` / `mobile friendly` diff guard can never fire again. Every
    preservation check in this plan would go green while protecting nothing. A rule addressed only to
    Tasks 2 and 3 does not cover that path; refusing to overwrite covers it regardless of which task
    re-runs, and regardless of why.

    **Recovery, if the guard fires.** Do NOT delete the directory to get past it. First establish
    whether any task has already edited the three documents (`git status --porcelain` on them, and
    `cmp -s` each against its `.before`). If nothing has been edited, the snapshot is still valid —
    reuse it and continue. Only if you are deliberately restarting the whole plan from a genuinely
    clean tree should you `rm -rf /tmp/gsd-01-17` and re-take it, and say so in the summary.

This plan changes no executable code, so the application's attack surface is unchanged. The threats
that apply are to the integrity of the records the project's future decisions rest on.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| prior verification pass → this reconciliation | Claims arrive as untrusted text; each must be re-derived rather than believed |
| this reconciliation → future readers | These four documents are what a later phase trusts instead of re-checking |
| human legs → recorded results | A result nobody observed must never enter the record as observed |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01-17-01 | Repudiation | `REQUIREMENTS.md` ticks and `01-VERIFICATION.md` status | high | mitigate | Ticking a box on unrun evidence converts an unverified claim into settled fact for every later phase, and nothing downstream re-derives it. Mitigated by the written decision table in Task 3, by the rule that a `human-owed` ledger row blocks its dependent tick, and by asserting ACCT-06 and ACCT-07 stay unticked with their reason recorded in the Traceability row itself. |
| T-01-17-02 | Tampering | scoped edits to long documents | high | mitigate | A whole-file `Write` on `REQUIREMENTS.md` or `01-UAT.md` silently destroys content outside the diff window — including accepted risks and prior analysis. Mitigated by the `Edit`-only override, by the diff-size acceptance criterion in Task 2, and by explicit greps proving `root_cause`, `partial_pass`, `reported`, the test-6 skip and the mobile deferral all survive. |
| T-01-17-03 | Information Disclosure | evidence ledger contents | low | accept | The ledger records commands and their outputs against local files. It must not paste secrets: the Google client id in `.env.local` is never read or recorded — plan 01-15's overrides state this and it carries here. |
| T-01-17-04 | Denial of Service | n/a | low | accept | No runtime surface is touched. |
| T-01-17-SC | Tampering | npm/pip/cargo installs | high | mitigate | This plan contains no package-manager install task and changes no application file. The gate is `git diff --stat -- . ':(exclude).planning'` being empty, asserted in all three tasks. |
